# YM35: 夹镜鸣琴 Jiajing Mingqin, "The Double Mirror and the Sound of the Lute"

Malone calls it Chia Ching Ming Ch'in.

Wave 2 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM35` · Page: `/scenes/#YM35` · Row: `research/buildings/YM35-jiajing-mingqin/`

## What it was

夹镜鸣琴 Jiajing Mingqin, on the south shore of 福海 west of 别有洞天: a double-eaved square bridge pavilion over the channel (E2003, S361), 聚远楼 Juyuan Lou to the south, 广育宫 Guangyu Gong to the east for the goddess 碧霞元君 with an archway in front and 凝祥殿 behind, then 南屏晚钟, 西山入画, 山容水态; west 湖山在望, 佳山水 and 洞里长春 (S05 j82:19b-20a). 西山入画 was rebuilt about 1763 as the five-bay 开鉴堂, later 渊渟镜澈 (E2003). Malone saw a deep well on the hill that fed the waterfall by hand (E1999, S02). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).

From the inventory row: **built** 雍正朝 (S43); Yongzheng; **changed** c. 道光十年 (1830): the natural-rock south shore of 福海 replaced by dressed-stone revetment, 463.36 m long, 2.24 m high above the base slab (one 浆板, four courses of large blocks, one cap course); three pavilions in the east rebuilt at the same time; **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S08, S43, S01, S361, S310).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Lyric of 1744 (to 水仙子): "取李青蓮兩水夾明鏡詩意架虹橋一道上搆傑閣俯瞰澄泓" (S05 j82:20b): after Li Bai's line on two waters holding a bright mirror, a rainbow bridge with a lofty pavilion on it, a cascade from the cliff beside, striking the rocks with the sound of a lute.
